💡 Key Takeaways
  • Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.
  • Industry observers note that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

Industry observers note that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

Recent findings suggest that "As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

It has been revealed that it goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

In a recent development, "Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

"Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

It has been revealed that the post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

Inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Sources indicate that those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

It has been revealed that the world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is right now the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?

It has been revealed that well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the company for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.

By retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.

It has been revealed that that lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents mentioned they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.

From Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees said that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.

It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.

Still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful launches lead to job cuts in recent years. As the manufacturer enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are at the moment voting on unionization.

Upcoming Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 Fresh Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too. If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely upcoming modes, the possibilities are vast.".

It has been revealed that the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, latest motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

Following last week‘s PlayStation 5 and PC pre-order launch, Switch 2 and Switch digital pre-orders for Professor Layton and the New World of Steam are now available for $64.99 / £53.99 / €64.99 / ¥7,920, LEVEL-5 announced. According to recent reports, as previously announced, pre-orders include the “Layton Series Soundtrack Selection,” a digital soundtrack featuring 11 pieces of music from the Professor Layton series. The tracks are accessible via the “Secret Content” menu in-game.

This upcoming adventure takes place one year after the events of Professor Layton and the Unwound Future.

The story unfolds in America, where the Wild West era has ended and the country is forging ahead into a latest age of development.

A letter from Luke leads Layton to Steam Bison, a town renowned for its inventions….

Recent findings suggest that steam Bison has undergone rapid technological advances thanks to the steam engine. But mysterious events are unfolding one after another, from a phantom gunman who has kidnapped a wealthy heiress to a gang of zombies threatening the town. Layton and Luke join forces once again to investigate these strange occurrences and embark on a grand puzzle-solving adventure.

◆ A Story That Unfolds as You Solve Puzzles.

You’ll encounter all kinds of puzzles as you explore the streets of Steam Bison.

—Even to meet Eggmuffin, an inventor, you’ll need to solve a puzzle to find the entrance to his room….

—Solve the puzzle, and the story moves forward.

◆ The Most Puzzles in Series History.

Recent findings suggest that layton and Luke face more puzzles than ever before in the series. Solve a wide variety of puzzles as you progress through the story and get to the bottom of the mysterious events unfolding in Steam Bison. Along the way, you’ll even come across puzzles that play a part in Steam Bison’s development. Solve them to upgrade the town’s facilities and watch the town flourish.

—Solve puzzles to develop facilities!

In a recent development, what’s more, a upcoming puzzle will be added to Daily Puzzles every day for over a year following launch. This lets you enjoy the game long after you’ve completed the story.

Whether you prefer to take your time solving puzzles on your own or gather around a major screen with family and friends to work them out together, that’s all part of the fun of the Layton series.

Stand Use snippets of conversation between café customers to recreate the drinks they ordered. Get the drinks right, and you might hear some juicy local gossip!

Recent findings suggest that use a mysterious device to transform ordinary items into treasure. Master its three modes: Reversal, Evolution, and Fusion!

The duck robot that monitors the factory won’t stop once it’s set in motion! Give it the right commands to overcome obstacles and complete the operational test.

In a recent development, experience Professor Layton and the Latest World of Steam in different languages! Choose your preferred languages for text and voice, and set off on an adventure with Professor Layton and Luke! Mix and match languages to experience the story in a whole new way!

Explore the Professor Layton games in the order their stories take place.

Professor Layton and the Latest World of Steam is due out for PlayStation 5, Switch 2, Switch, and PC via Steam on December 10.

Industry observers note that the level of talent on Season 30 of NBC’s long-running singing competition The Voice, currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule, is undeniable. The cuts have been "brutal," and some really incredible singers already went home before the Live Demonstrates even started. The success of the show isn’t solely about the contestants. We also tune in to for the fun coach interactions, all of which has been noticeably absent during the live performances, disappointingly so.

Honestly, this is a problem that's typical with The Voice during live reveals, but I'd forgotten given the network dropped them for Season 29. As the competition narrows and the numbers of remaining singers gets smaller, I hope there will be an opportunity for this to return. Let's talk it out.

Earlier this season, Kelly Clarkson and newbie Riley Green really upped The Voice coach prank game. Whether it was a personalized gift from the American Idol winner attempting to help a fellow coach get over losing top-notch singers during the Blind Auditions, or it was the country music superstar using his duck call for a laugh, those moments have been glaringly lacking from the Live Shows.

Recent findings suggest that honestly, the biggest disappointment of the Live Highlights doesn’t have anything to do with the performances themselves. There hasn’t been a bad performance. It instead comes from the fact that the episodes breeze by so swiftly that there hasn’t been time for coach banter or any of the silly moments that we’ve come to love.

Sources indicate that again, this season has been particularly fun with Clarkson’s zany antics, including trying to give a contestant her hair, and Green never missing the chance to poke fun at Adam Levine’s age. It also would have been the perfect opportunity for Adam to throw it in Riley’s face (or at least console him) that his team still has three singers left while the latter only has two.

Sources indicate that don’t get me wrong, the Live Demonstrates have seen all the contestants step up as they perform with musicians and back-up singers while vying for viewer votes. But the lack of coach banter is an obvious and unfortunate mistake that I hope the show fixes soon.

With the Blind Auditions, Battles, and Cut Week having two-hour episodes, cutting the Live Indicates to one hour doesn’t even allow for much coach commentary and feedback. To me that's a big problem. When it comes time to announce which singers have made it through for another week and who’s going to be sent home, there’s barely the time to even say goodbye, right?

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Sources indicate that so, then it becomes just another instance of shaving time away from the coaches. While it’s been stated that the Live Demonstrates were brought back by demand from the fans, it feels like there’s a better way that it could have been handled so that it didn’t feel so jarring. Like maybe finding a happy medium with 90-minute episodes? Survivor does it!

You can keep following along with the competition on NBC on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET, or stream the next day with a Peacock subscription, until the winner is declared in December. The competition series will then be shaking things up with Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity with fresh host Keke Palmer, and I hope that version will keep the coach banter game going.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

According to recent reports, the stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One million copies for each month on sale, it seems.
  • That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.
  • In a recent development, slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.

That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

In a recent development, slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It quickly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

Recent findings suggest that it was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen said.

Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March.

Slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a new character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active consumers to reach its highest daily player count in six months.

Industry observers note that "Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours.".

Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.

Recent findings suggest that looking ahead, Slay the Spire 2's road to version 1.0 is expected to be long, with several features and gameplay additions still in the works. Then there are the console ports, which have yet to be unveiled, but are very much expected.

In Eurogamer's Slay the Spire 2 early access review, Bertie Purchese called it "a deceptively familiar sequel" whose confident design and smart new additions build on what made the original work so well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, whether you're looking for GTA 6 safe codes for story missions or just for grabbing some quick cash around Leonida, you can find over 50 safes in GTA 6. Some of these are locked with codes and others can be broken into, with the former typically offering larger rewards.Unfortunately, aside from safes you come across in story missions and major side quests, most safe codes are randomized, but I can at least help you there by guiding you on how to obtain them. Either way, you've got a few options at your disposal when it comes to cracking safes in GTA 6, so here's everything you need to know.

There are two methods of getting GTA 6 safe codes:.

Recent findings suggest that which you'll need depends on the location, but by using your Focus by pressing down on L3 and R3/LS and RS, you can highlight the location of the safe code if there is one. If you can't see one, you probably need to threaten the staff by holding down the LT/L2 button and then press X/Square to threaten. Eventually, the threaten option will turn into a 'Safe code?' option, as seen in the image above. The Avery Pawn Shop GTA 6 safe code is an example of one of these, so why not use that to try it out.Alternatively, safes that require a code can be blown open using sticky bombs. These are only unlocked once you reach the Credit Checked mission in Chapter 3, but as I've explained in my dedicated guide to getting into the Kingpin Bowling safe in GTA 6, there are a few you can pick up at the alley - and presumably other places around the GTA 6 map - before you unlock them at Ammu-Nation.

These are the set GTA 6 safe codes that are the same for every player:.

According to recent reports, aside from the 0420 safe code that's given to you in Chapter 1, there are three main safe codes you'll need when gathering funds in GTA 6, and they're all related to the Kolt gang in Port Gellhorn. All three codes are found in the same place, Brooks Boatworks, but since they're set, you can use them from our list above without having to go looking for them. This won't save you a lot of trouble, though, as you'll still have to get past the gang in all three locations anyway.

There then appear to be a handful of other safe codes that aren't randomized, due to the nature of how you find the code, and I'll add those to the list above as I find them.

The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1225 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, while pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. We got all the deals, baby!).

In a recent development, while pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?

Recent findings suggest that “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. The phrase gradually caught on. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the New York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

But even before it had a name, Black Friday was a thing. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas.” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Big Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

Recent findings suggest that A more modern matter with the name is that Black Friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-November and bleeding over into the following Saturday, Sunday, “Cyber Monday,” Tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “Do you want to go Black Friday shopping this Sunday?” So far, alternative names like “Five-Day Frenzy” and “The day I get to trample someone to save $8 on a Nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

In a recent development, beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of Black Friday shopping to Thursday (aka Thanksgiving Day). Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p.m. on Thursday. The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

The term “Cyber Monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the Monday after Thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. The term first appeared on Nov. 28, 2005, in a Shop.org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Promptly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. Americans spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

It has been revealed that if all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

According to recent reports, it’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. On the other hand, maybe substantial retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Sure.

Recent findings suggest that depending on how you measure it, Black Friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a significant box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

Sources indicate that I mean, yeah, of course. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a latest TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—substantial-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out swiftly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

In a recent development, yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, Black Friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million Americans in one way or another. What that says about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.

According to recent reports, nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the tech giant and AMERICA.

In a recent development, "On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones noted during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

Industry observers note that that last bit seems likely to have been stated with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "fresh standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the tech giant’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the firm's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

"No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a fresh generation of video game narrative designers.

"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.".

Her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

In a recent development, "The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV demonstrates and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

Industry observers note that we know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.

In a recent development, the man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.

It has been revealed that to change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed.

According to recent reports, this doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.

It's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.

There's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.

While you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • Sources indicate that BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

Sources indicate that BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it notes on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Confirmed in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

Recent findings suggest that the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The firm grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - founded by ex-GTA veteran - has a mountain of debt, and the main plan for paying it back is litigation

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the firm created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt.
  • This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back.
  • "Prior to the Firm's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the firm created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the manufacturer's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

"Prior to the Firm's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

"The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions.".

This tallies with the narrative spun by co-firm leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard mentioned.

According to recent reports, the situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "major American company" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

Industry observers note that it had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it released, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

Build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was unveiled in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that as you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

In a recent development, "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a new patch - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

It has been revealed that "If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear.".

According to recent reports, "If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong.".

Though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

"She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY.".

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese company makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

According to recent reports, so far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr stated it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 is set 80 years after the events of 1982 sci-fi classic Blade Runner, but despite the Replicant-filled world undergoing some radical changes in the intervening decades, the Prime Video show's creator turned to Ridley Scott for clarification on a number of canon questions.

It has been revealed that scott, of course, directed Blade Runner and is an executive producer on Blade Runner 2099. So when 2099 showrunner Silka Luisa had questions about the history of the cyberpunk world, there was only one place to turn. "He's such an idol for me. It was like meeting a rock star," Luisa tells GamesRadar+. "He had so much insight into the first film, because so much of it is off-screen your imagination just takes over, but there's a lot of open questions intentionally, right? It's very ambiguous.

According to recent reports, "So when I went to go write," Luisa continues. "I realized that the canon is not concrete, and so it's hard to build on top of that foundation when you're not sure if what you're saying is accurate or not. And so, what was really helpful with Ridley was being able to ask him: What I thought this meant – is this correct? What did you think Off-world was? Where did you think the Replicants came from? Tell me about Tyrell; how did you imagine him? I mean, just as a fan, they're the questions you would be dying to have answered. But also from a practical sense, as a writer, I just needed to know. I needed the Bible for our show, and that was Ridley.".

Industry observers note that this makes sense – Scott is perhaps the only person to have played a major creative role in all three live-action Blade Runner projects, as he was also an executive producer on 2017's Denis Villeneuve-directed Blade Runner 2049. And unlike Star Wars, Game of Thrones, the MCU, and many storytelling sandboxes, there is no one person or group that is the arbiter of canon in the Blade Runner universe. Instead, it's up to the creators of each individual project to forge ahead, which could become a problem when looking back.

Recent findings suggest that it's safe to say, then, that Blade Runner 2099 will have one eye on the past, while looking to the future. Starring Michelle Yeoh as Replicant Olwen, and Hunter Schafer as a human Cora, Blade Runner 2099 is set in the aftermath of a Replicant revolt that saw synthetic humans rise to power and humans subjugated. Bad news for Cora, who must go undercover at the LAPD to win freedom for her and her brother. The final trailer is out now.

While it's not ignoring canon, we do know that Blade Runner 2099 is "not directly connected" to Blade Runner 2049, and won't directly pick up on the events of that movie, as it's designed to "stand alone". And while a second season of Blade Runner 2099 is unlikely, as the 8-episode show is already being billed as a "limited series", franchise producers Alcon Entertainment have suggested a AAA Blade Runner video game is in the works.

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

In a recent development, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

According to recent reports, raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

In a recent development, gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the latest team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

#40261. Breaking: You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

Breaking: You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them.
  • Sources indicate that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress.
  • It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

Sources indicate that you can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a upcoming manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a big heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," indicates David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style.".

Recent findings suggest that that means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," notes Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

According to recent reports, in the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here. If you want to, ahem, 'travel to Upcoming Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a first substantial patch since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database.
  • "We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick enhancement on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.
  • There are two main upcoming features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a first substantial patch since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick enhancement on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

There are two main upcoming features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that shows off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

Recent findings suggest that "We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you.".

In a recent development, that seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

"We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region.".

Recent findings suggest that folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

Beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how rapidly the team can react to concerns have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively new custodians of both it and SteamDB.

Now it is finally coming to Nintendo Switch!

Saihate Station: Twilight Edition includes the main game, the downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” and two mini-games, all in one package.

“After falling asleep on the last train, I woke up in a bizarre place called Saihate Station…”.

Sources indicate that haru Akinashi is a self-effacing office worker who lacks confidence and fails at everything he tries. Having slept through his stop on the last train, he finds himself trapped in a bizarre place called Saihate Station, where gruesome supernatural phenomena occur.

Shion Tatsunami is his complete opposite: a cheerful, talented colleague and former friend—happens to be there as well, and the two promise to work together to return home.

Their interactions are awkward at first, given the estrangement, but with each problem they overcome together, Haru recalls their former friendship, and their bond grows stronger than before.

Then, the truth of the world closes in.

It has been revealed that the main game features four multiple-ending story routes. The ending branches based on fluctuations in Haru’s “dependency level,” which changes according to the player’s actions.

In a recent development, starting November 20, pre-orders for the physical edition will begin sequentially at retailers in Japan. As a first-print bonus, a “shaka-shaka acrylic stand keychain” featuring a train and character motif will be included. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you've been online at all today, you'll know that what feels like the entire world is at the moment fawning over GTA 6. As the reviews dropped, one thing swiftly became very clear: this is a game absolutely packed with detail. Our own Chris noted that, thanks to this focus on specific detail and unbelievable nuance, Grand Theft Auto 6 is "the most unbelievable video game world ever made". And it's no accident: this is something Rockstar put a lot of dedicated effort into.

It's been well-established that the studio has gone above and beyond to make this interactive world one of the most richly-developed we've ever seen: Rockstar has told us it "re-engineered" its weather systems to "achieve a sense of scale we haven't felt before," adding hurricanes, rainbows and heavy rain. It simulated and built a complex drug system, allowing Lucia and Jason to partake in drug use "directly from their inventory" and "at any time". But there are still details emerging from the dev team that are blowing my mind. And the most recent byte of information I saw was related to how Rockstar worked with sound.

"Much of the dynamic soundscape is informed by the incredibly detailed art throughout the world," explains Alastair MacGregor, vice president of audio at Rockstar. "One small example is that convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect. As a result, the bottles behind the doors can be heard shaking and the units click on and off more frequently. In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment.".

This level of detail is, quite frankly, absurd. It's a testament to granularity Rockstar is willing to go to in making Leonida feel truly lived-in and realistic. And this level of production isn't restricted to internal locations, either. "On the ambient side, we love the contrast between the manicured luxury islands, with the sizzle of crickets and lawn sprinklers backed by birdsong, yacht halyards clanging in the distance, and yard work going on, versus urban areas with the sounds of people living on top of each other - snatches of every genre of music, distant voices, cars peeling out, construction, the omnipresent hum of elderly air conditioners struggling with the humidity," continues MacGregor.

He goes on to say that if you're wandering the streets of Gellhorn - a coastal city in Kelly County on the western side of Leonida - it's acoustically a very different vibe than the high-rise centre of Vice City, where the sound bounces between the buildings. This means that the engine is handling not just the sounds of things as minute as bugs in the grass, but also how that sound travels, and interacts with other physical entities in the world. "We've spent years iterating on reverb technology to make sure that you can feel that - from the pops of cars backfiring to the wash of a helicopter passing by overhead to birds squawking in the trees," concludes MacGregor.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 launches tomorrow - Thursday, 19th November - for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It's also worth noting that Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

"It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 releases on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off
